name: Pack a backpack efficiently
blurb: Load carrying is a comfort skill: the same weight feels dramatically lighter when it is placed correctly, and the same pack fits far better once you understand the belt-to-shoulder handover.
gear: Your pack and your actual kit
steps: Weigh everything and write the list out. You cannot pack well what you have not measured.
Load by zone: heavy items — water, food, stove — against your back at shoulder-blade height; medium items around them; sleeping bag and light bulk at the bottom.
Fill dead space so nothing shifts, and keep the load symmetrical left to right.
Put what you need on the move in the lid and hipbelt pockets: waterproof, snacks, map, hat.
Fit it properly: hipbelt on the iliac crest first, take 70–80% of the weight there, then tighten shoulder straps and load lifters, then the sternum strap.
Walk with it loaded, adjust, and repack anything you never touched.
tips: Heavy items low is a myth for hiking packs — heavy and close to your spine, at mid-back height, carries best.
Anything strapped to the outside will snag, swing or get lost. Put it inside.
Line the pack with a dry bag rather than trusting a rain cover.
proof: You pack for a two-night trip, reach everything you need without unpacking, and finish the walk without shoulder pain.
